notes.meaning: God's people are called to sing a fresh song of praise because He has done astonishing things to rescue them. The phrase 'right hand and holy arm' pictures God acting in pure holiness and power without any human help. He alone won the victory over the powers of sin, death, and evil.

The Lord has not kept His saving work a secret hidden away in one small corner. Instead, He has openly displayed His salvation and shown His righteous character to all the surrounding nations. God's good news is meant to be seen and known by the whole world.

God remembered the ancient covenant promises of mercy and truth that He made to the people of Israel. Because He stayed completely faithful to Israel, the blessing of His salvation has now spread to the ends of the earth. His faithfulness to one nation opened the door of rescue for all humanity.

The call now goes out to the entire earth to burst into loud, joyful song before the Lord. Words pile up here to urge believers to sing with hearty enthusiasm and real energy, not in a half-hearted or sleepy way. Celebrating God's great redemption deserves our loudest and most joyful shouts.

Worshipers are invited to bring every kind of sound before the Lord, combining the gentle melody of harps with the bold blast of horns and trumpets. In the temple, these instruments welcomed the presence of God as the true Sovereign. Blending musical sweetness and power shows the deep joy of hailing the Lord as King.

differ.view: Some historically believed that musical instruments belonged to Old Testament temple shadows and should not be used in church worship.

notes.meaning: The psalm turns from human voices and invites the physical world to join in the chorus of praise. The roaring seas sound like rolling thunder, the rushing rivers seem to clap like hands against their banks, and the hills sing out together. All of nature is pictured as rejoicing under the care of its Creator.

Creation rejoices because the Lord is coming to rule and bring justice to the earth. Unlike human rulers who can be unfair or easily bribed, God will judge with pure righteousness and fairness. His coming rule brings hope and comfort to everyone who longs for wrongs to be made right.
